newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai Industrial sees asset hike soon.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Industrial sees asset hike soon.

text.p: Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd expects to complete plans for an asset injection by the year-end, a senior official said on Monday.
Chen Weishu, executive director of corporate parent Shanghai Industrial Investment (Holdings) Co Ltd, also said that the company was considering several possible financing plans.
"It will be a substantial size," he said of the asset injection.
"We are looking at four or five different financing strategies including bank loans and the use of internal funds," he told reporters at an investment seminar.
He did not name any of the assets but said that a number of firms would be purchased from the Shanghai government and injected into the Hong Kong-listed vehicle.
Shanghai Industrial already has operations in tobacco, pharmaceuticals, personal care products and printing.
It has been a closely followed stock since it made its impressive debut on the Hong Kong exchange in May.

It closed at HK$17.10 on Friday compared with its debut of HK$8 and its offer price of HK$7.28. There was no trading in Hong Kong on Monday though speculation over the asset injection has been buoying the shares of late.
Chen said that the injected assets would be in consumer goods, retailing, basic industries and the automotive sector.
Some analysts have raised fears that the assets might include some unprofitable companies that the Shanghai government wanted to get rid of.
"All will be commercial deals," he said. "All of them will be making money."
